reason: The text explicitly depicts Pharaoh (the political elite) deliberately increasing hardship on the Israelites (regular people). When Moses and Aaron request permission for the people to leave, Pharaoh refuses and then deliberately escalates their suffering by commanding overseers to stop providing straw for brick-making while maintaining production quotas (וַיְצַ֥ו פַּרְעֹ֖ה...לֹ֣א תֹאסִפ֞וּן לָתֵ֨ת תֶּ֧בֶן). The narrative shows the overseers (נֹגְשִׂים) actively pressuring the enslaved people, and Pharaoh explicitly hardening his heart against their plight. The elite's intentional infliction of suffering on those without power is the central narrative element of this passage.
